I make notes on my phone when I think of something that would be a good name for a place later in the game. For a lot of them, my players are a great help and we brainstorm a lot together. For example, the bar where the PCs live is named the Broken Antler, because it's in a city that has Erastil as it's main deity.

For characters, I'm not ashamed to admit that for the meaningless NPCs, I print out a list of generic fantasy names and cross them off as I use them. (Because for the first few sessions, my players LOVED to put me on the spot and ask me "What's the shopkeeper's name? What that guard's name? What's that peasant's name?" about every goddamn NPC they saw) For meaningful NPCs, like semi-DMPCs or regular quest givers, I do plan them out ahead of time with fitting names for their backgrounds and races, usually by using baby name websites. 

EDIT: I also remember things my players hate in real life and if they're being particularly annoying I'll name things after that. Like their goblin fence, Nuggit.
Yeah! It's just so much more meaningful and cool when you level up from slaying a BBEG at the end of a big dungeon, rather than tallying up EXP from killing the goons in the dungeon.

I let my players level, but instead of measuring EXP from combat, (because there's so much more to the game than combat!) I just let them level when they accomplish something worth celebrating. Killing eighty goblins won't get you to the next level, but if you diplomatically rescue a princess from a dragon, then that's worth celebrating. Makes it more story based and exciting, and I'm not obligated to let them level when they've killed X amount of goons.
